cohort_definition: Citadel Securities (the market-making firm, distinct from the Citadel hedge fund) entry-level cohorts, kept separate: (a) Quantitative Trading interns, (b) Quantitative Research interns (BS/MS and PhD tracks), and (c) Software Engineering interns. All are 11-week summer internships, June-August, per official postings.
sample_size_note: No licensed population sample used. Curated-qualitative CIR from public sources only (Doc 3 §1.6 Phase 1); no cohort percentages are stated because none were sourced.

school_dist.claim: Citadel Securities publishes no school distribution for these cohorts. Omitted rather than estimated.

prior_employer_dist.claim: Entry-level intern cohorts: postings ask for degree progress and skills, not prior employers. The QR BS/MS posting does ask for prior experience in a data-driven research environment and independent research experience — research track record, not a named feeder employer.

major_dist.claim: Quantitative Trading interns: bachelor's or master's in applied math, engineering, statistical modeling, computer science, physics or related disciplines (official posting).
Quantitative Research interns (BS/MS): mathematics, statistics, physics, computer science or another highly quantitative field (official posting).
Software Engineering interns: bachelor's, master's or PhD in computer science, computer engineering or related fields (official posting).

skills_dist.claim: Trading: systematic, quantitative thinking under uncertainty; programming/scripting/statistical software strongly preferred; passion for markets.

Research: probability and statistics including machine learning, time-series analysis, pattern recognition and NLP; translating models into code in Python, R or C++; backtesting and implementing trading models/signals.
Engineering: exceptional programming and design skills, analytical skill with probability/statistics familiarity, and building high-performance, large-data research platforms.

path_patterns.pattern: 11-week summer internship (June-August) in trading, research or engineering -> full-time entry role (conversion terms are not published in the postings used)
Degree-level split inside research: BS/MS analyst track and a separate PhD researcher track, with distinct postings

entry_routes.who_it_fits: BS/MS students in math, statistics, physics, CS or similar, with data-driven research experience

hiring_bar_summary: The bar the firm itself publishes is a degree in a short list of quantitative disciplines plus demonstrable probability/statistics depth and (for research and trading) coding. Notably, the official postings do NOT name competition results (olympiads, Putnam) as requirements, and this record does not claim them as screens: that claim is common in folklore but was not stated by the firm in sources used. Candidate reports (anecdotal) describe probability, expected-value and market-making games as the lived interview reality.

screening_signals.claim: Ability to think systematically and quantitatively and to deal with uncertainty in a rigorous, statistical way — stated verbatim in substance across the trading and research postings.
For research: independent research experience and prior work in a data-driven research environment are explicit stated signals.

process_stages.claim: Firm-published trading interview structure (from Citadel Securities' own prep materials): Step 1 phone screen (about 45 minutes with a trading-team member: background, interest, technical questions); Step 2 onsite/Zoom interviews with several traders, largely technical; Step 3 offer stage with recruitment.

Candidate reports (anecdotal, Glassdoor) frequently describe an online assessment in probability/mental math before interviews for trading roles; the firm postings used here do not themselves specify an assessment, so this is labeled reported, not firm-stated.

interview_styles.claim: Technical and behavioral, built around sample problems in the firm's own published prep topics: expected value, confidence intervals, market making and options basics; the firm tells candidates to study these overviews before interviews.
Anecdotal candidate reports add: fast card/coin probability games and dynamic market-making games in live rounds.

values_culture_signals.claim: The firm describes itself as a technology-driven, next-generation global market maker whose engineers, traders and researchers work in small teams with short development cycles and work that rapidly reaches production.

hiring_cadence: Internships are an 11-week signature summer program, June-August, per official postings (occasionally flexible at other times of year). Postings for the next summer's class were live on the official careers site at verification (October 2026); exact application open/close dates are not published in the postings used and must be checked on the live board each cycle.

compensation_notes.note: No compensation figure is stated: sampled official Citadel Securities intern postings did not publish a salary range. (Salary ranges seen on the separate Citadel hedge-fund site belong to a different legal employer and were deliberately not imported.)

referral_weight_notes: No firm-published statement on referral weight was found. Anecdotal candidate reports show most applicants arriving via online application, with referrals a minority route; that is candidate self-report data, not a firm policy, and is not weighted here.
red_flags: Confusing Citadel Securities with Citadel (the hedge fund): different firms, different postings, different roles — salary and program details do not transfer between them.

Folklore risk: competition-medal requirements are widely asserted for quant firms generally; Citadel Securities' own postings used here do not state them, so do not self-screen out (or in) on that basis alone.
Interview-prep claims from third-party coaching sites are not firm statements; the firm's own published prep topics are the reliable list.
thesis_text: Bottom line: Citadel Securities runs one of the cleanest undergraduate quant doors — provided your degree and skills match a short, published list. The firm hires three separate entry cohorts: quant trading interns (applied math, engineering, statistics, CS, physics or similar), quant research interns split into BS/MS and PhD tracks, and software engineering interns (CS/CE). What the firm says it screens for is unusually explicit: rigorous statistical thinking under uncertainty, probability and statistics depth (machine learning and time-series for research), and the ability to turn models into code in Python, R or C++. Its own interview-prep materials name the game plainly — expected value, confidence intervals, market making and options — through a trader phone screen and then largely technical rounds. Ranked routes: (1) the 11-week summer internship in your exact cohort, applied to early in the cycle; (2) if you are a researcher, build the independent, data-driven research record the BS/MS and PhD postings explicitly ask for; (3) if you are an engineer, the SWE internship is a genuinely separate door with a CS/CE degree screen and a probability/statistics familiarity bonus. Do not import hedge-fund Citadel facts into this firm, and do not treat medal folklore as a stated requirement — the published bar is degrees, probability, and code.
known_biases_of_data: Built only from public firm pages, official postings and credible public reporting. No LinkedIn or logged-in data (Doc 3 §1.1). Firm-published program statistics are marketing-adjacent and self-reported; interview details from candidate-report sites are anecdotal and labeled as such. Survivorship bias applies: sources describe who is hired, not who applied and failed.
